data.why: A river in its own valley (terrain with a riverbed, a river in it from the first frame), a toy boat drifting down it. The weight's path is the story: a plank snaps, a slab on piers cracks, an arch over a frame pushes the piers apart, packed stone holds them, a flood slams the solid piers, flood arches let it through, the rushing water digs the riverbed out, riprap stones fix it; the cart rolls across at the end. The camera opens on the plank, then holds the bridge's front with the river in section.

ideas.idea: a plank laid across a river is already a bridge
a loaded cart is too heavy and the plank snaps
stone piers on both banks with a stone slab across
the long slab bends under the weight and cracks
wedge stones curved over a wooden frame make an arch that is only squeezed
the arch pushes outward and shoves the piers apart
heavy stone packed behind the piers holds them
the heavy solid piers now block a spring flood, which slams into them
flood arches through the piers let the floodwater pass
the water rushing through digs the riverbed out from under the piers
big stones piled round the pier feet stop the digging
paved road and walls: a cart rolls across over the river
you have built a stone arch bridge

chain.shows: the loaded cart rolls on and the plank snaps in two
chain.stakes: the cart falls in the river

chain.shows: the long stone slab cracks in the middle under a heavy block
without its frame the arch pushes the piers apart
a flood rises to the arch and slams into the heavy piers, lifting a boat
chain.stakes: the whole bridge is pushed over

chain.shows: water rushing through the flood arches digs out the riverbed and the piers sink
chain.stakes: the bridge sinks into the river

recurring.what: a toy boat drifting down the river

surprises.claim: Roman arch stones were held up during building on a temporary wooden frame called centering, removed once the keystone was set
surprises.search: Roman arch bridge wooden centering removed after keystone

surprises.claim: An arch pushes outward on its supports (thrust), so its ends need heavy abutments to stop them spreading
surprises.search: arch thrust pushes outward abutments resist spreading

surprises.claim: Some Roman bridges have small flood openings through their piers so floodwater can pass, as in the Pons Fabricius in Rome
surprises.search: Pons Fabricius flood opening in pier

surprises.claim: Scour, the riverbed washing away around piers, is the most common cause of bridge failure
surprises.search: scour most common cause of bridge failure

sentences.text: If you lay a plank across a river, you have a bridge.
But a loaded cart snaps the plank.
So you lay a slab on stone piers.
But under the weight, the long slab cracks.
So you curve wedge stones over a wooden frame.
But without the frame, the arch pushes the piers apart.
So you pack heavy stone behind each pier.
But a flood rises and pounds against the piers.
So you open a flood arch through each pier.
But water rushing through digs out the riverbed.
So you pile big stones around their feet.
Pave the road, and a cart rolls across the river.
Congratulations, you have built an arch bridge.
